gap: Acceptance check for A: in this sidewalk framing, the side away from the road must show continuous, lit ground-floor shopfronts (glazing with visible interior content) across at least 25% of the frame width. Within about 15 m of the camera there must be at least 3 distinct legible signs or practical light sources (blade/neon sign, awning, lit poster) and at least 3 pavement props (A-frame board, bin, bench, poster case or bollard), so the pavement reads as a downtown street rather than an empty path between trees.

Judge: B wins all four pairs clearly; none is close. The B frames have art-directed lighting and time of day (neon at blue hour, pink-lit dusk, a hazy night meet, crisp high-contrast noon), sharp material response (clear-coat and chrome reflections, worn asphalt with debris), dense set dressing (signage, posters, branded props, signals, palms, landmarks) and staged groups of people doing things. Their low, tilted or layered cameras also give them a strong composition advantage, but even with composition set aside they win on lighting, materials and set dressing. The four A frames share the same faults. Many identical tree instances repeat. The skylines are boxes with tiled windows. The light is flat and slightly overexposed, with heavy sun bloom. Vehicles and near ground surfaces look soft. Pedestrians look like stock models with flat shading and similar gaits, walking in lanes or single file rather than interacting. Sidewalks have no shopfronts, signs or street props. The player's back takes the centre of every frame, and the HUD is placeholder-grade: a rectangle minimap, an ammo counter with no weapon, and a pedestrian clipping the frame edge in pair 1. A does have a coherent city layout, decent pedestrian and traffic counts, and readable local identity (plates, taxi, keep-left sign, landmark domes, hawker centre); pair 3 A is its best frame. The fixes most likely to close the gap, in order: lit, dressed street frontage with signs and pavement props; sharp vehicle and near-ground materials with real reflections and contact shadows; pedestrian behaviour that is varied and grouped around a focal point; and a stronger lighting and time-of-day grade with depth haze in place of flat noon bloom. B wows in pairs 1 and 3. No A frame wows.
